definition: Artificial intelligence is used by many different businesses and organizations.
details: It is widely used in the financial sector, especially by accounting firms, to help detect fraud. In 2022, PricewaterhouseCoopers reported that fraud has impacted 46% of all businesses in the world. The shift from working in person to working from home has brought increased access to data. According to an FTC (Federal Trade Commission) study from 2022, customers reported fraud of approximately $5.8 billion in 2021, an increase of 70% from the year before. The majority of these scams were imposter scams and online shopping frauds. Furthermore, artificial intelligence plays a crucial role in developing advanced algorithms and machine learning models that enhance fraud detection systems, enabling businesses to stay ahead of evolving fraudulent tactics in an increasingly digital landscape.

explainer.lead: Artificial intelligence in fraud detection means using algorithms and machine learning models to help organizations spot suspicious activity. It matters because fraud is widespread and costly, and detection systems must keep up as fraudulent tactics change.

tiers.eli5: Banks and companies use computers to spot strange patterns in transactions, like a guard who notices something odd before money is lost.
tiers.practitioner: It is applied to flagging fraud in financial-sector data; a pitfall is that the shift to remote work increased access to data, and scams rose 70% year over year in 2021 according to FTC customer reports of about $5.8 billion.
tiers.paperLevel: The literature records deployment in financial-sector and accounting fraud detection; PricewaterhouseCoopers reported in 2022 that fraud had impacted 46% of all businesses worldwide, with imposter scams making up the majority of reported cases.

explainer.example: A business runs customer activity through a machine learning model in its fraud detection system. The model flags a pattern associated with an imposter scam, allowing the business to investigate that activity instead of treating it as routine.

explainer.intuition: Fraudulent activity can leave warning signs in data, and AI helps organizations find those signs at scale. Its value is not just spotting known scams, but strengthening detection as tactics change.
howItWorks: Gather activity data that the organization can lawfully access and analyze.
Use algorithms or machine learning models to examine that activity.
Identify activity that appears suspicious enough for the detection system to flag.
Update the detection approach as fraudulent tactics evolve.
explainer.whyItMatters: PricewaterhouseCoopers reported in 2022 that fraud had affected 46% of businesses worldwide. An FTC study from 2022 said customers reported approximately $5.8 billion in fraud losses in 2021, up 70% from the previous year, with imposter scams and online shopping fraud making up the majority of these scams.
misconceptions: AI fraud detection is not limited to banks; accounting firms and many other businesses and organizations use it.
A detection system is not finished once it is built, because fraudulent tactics continue to evolve.
Increased access to data from remote work does not by itself detect fraud; algorithms and models are still needed.

diagram.caption: AI models turn activity data into fraud signals, while changing tactics create an ongoing need to adapt detection.
